extracted.intended_audience: scholars and organizations preparing NEH Collaborative Research grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility/expectations for organizational teams applying to the NEH Collaborative Research program, including topical limits, required outputs, collaboration expectations, budget and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program topical focus (2026–27 limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026-27 Collaborative Research competition will be limited to projects on American history or culture or Western civilization. Applications must focus on topics in the history and culture of the United States in any period from the Colonial Era to the present, or topics in Western civilization from antiquity to the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure project subject matter falls within these topical boundaries for the 2026–27 cycle; proposals outside these topics are ineligible for this competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangible and sustainable outputs requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed projects must aim to result in tangible and sustainable outputs, such as a co-authored or multi-authored book, an edited volume, a themed issue of a peer-reviewed journal, or a series of peer-reviewed articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH expects concrete, durable interpretive products rather than only ephemeral activities; applicants should describe how the proposed output will be produced and sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration and interpretive product
rubrics_metrics.description: The Collaborative Research program aims to advance humanistic knowledge by supporting teams of scholars working on a joint project leading to a tangible interpretive product. All project outputs must incorporate collaboration and interpretation to address significant humanities research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should show genuine team-based collaboration and how interpretation is a central feature of the deliverable (not merely an administrative compilation). Describe roles, joint intellectual contributions, and collaborative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams may propose research in a single field of study or interdisciplinary work. Collaborators may come from one or more institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary teams are allowed and may include collaborators across institutions; the proposal should justify the team makeup and how the mix of fields advances the humanistic aims of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanistic content and methods requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH encourages partnerships with researchers in the natural and social sciences, but projects must focus on humanistic content and employ humanistic methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when including non-humanities partners, the project’s central questions, approaches, and interpretation must remain grounded in humanities scholarship; methodological balance should be explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: International collaboration with U.S. contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: International collaboration is welcome, but scholars at U.S. institutions must contribute significantly to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing international partners, document the substantial substantive role of U.S.-based scholars and ensure compliance with any NEH expectations about domestic contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged intellectual qualities: multiple viewpoints and new inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH encourages projects that incorporate multiple points of view and pursue new avenues of inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate how the project brings diverse perspectives and advances novel questions or methods in the humanities rather than repeating well-trodden approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible/expected output types (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected Output: Book; Themed Issue of Peer-Reviewed Journal. Proposed projects must aim to result in tangible and sustainable outputs, such as a co-authored or multi-authored book, an edited volume, a themed issue of a peer-reviewed journal, or a series of peer-reviewed articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples as models for acceptable final products; indicate the target form(s) of dissemination and any partner journals/publishers or plans for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and period limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award amount: Depending on funding category, up to $250,000. Period of performance: Up to three years (Depending on funding category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare budgets and timelines consistent with these ceilings; note that limits may vary by funding category, so consult the Notice of Funding Opportunity for category-specific caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions outlined in the Notice of Funding Opportunity. Submit your application package on Grants.gov. Register for an account with SAM.gov and Grants.gov; both are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and current SAM.gov and Grants.gov registrations are mandatory before submission. Applicants will receive multiple confirmations from Grants.gov; verify receipt of all confirmations. Prepare PDFs (download Adobe Reader; follow tips for making PDFs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to read NOFO and program resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and are prepared to write the most effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult program resources (Frequently Asked Questions, List of Recent Awards, Sample Application Narratives, Planning International Collaboration, Manuscript Preparation) to shape competitive proposals and conform to NEH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on the use of artificial intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow NEH’s AI policy when preparing proposals; consult the linked policy document for permitted/required disclosures and limits on AI-generated content.
